vignette: Ali is a 34-year-old Middle Eastern man married to his high school sweetheart, Leila. He works as a publisher in New York City and has been struggling with intrusive thoughts and feelings since a traumatic event that occurred six months ago. On a sunny afternoon, while walking home from work, Ali witnessed an armed assailant brutally attack Leila near their apartment building. Though she survived, the physical and psychological toll on both of them was immense. The trauma left deep scars in Ali’s mind. He now experiences fragmented memories of the event that come to him as disconnected pieces rather than a coherent narrative. Often, he hears voices in his head, echoing the terrifying sounds from that day—screams and the metallic clatter of weapons. These auditory intrusions are particularly vivid when he feels very tired or exhausted, which happens frequently since the attack due to his disrupted sleep patterns. Ali’s triggers have become potent reminders of that harrowing day. The vulnerability associated with being naked is a constant fear for him; he worries about Leila’s safety whenever she goes out alone and feels an overwhelming sense of responsibility to protect her. Public transport, especially riding the bus, has become unbearable due to his heightened anxiety. He fears crowded spaces where potential threats are harder to predict. His threat monitoring behaviors are pervasive. Ali constantly studies people's faces and body language for signs of danger, always on edge, scanning environments for any potential weapons or dangerous objects. This hyper-vigilance extends to his avoidance of unfamiliar places; he feels a profound sense of unease in new settings where assessing the level of risk is challenging. These behaviors have taken a toll on Ali’s life and work. His daily commute has become a source of immense stress, leading him to frequently arrive at the office exhausted. This fatigue often impacts his productivity and focus during meetings. He has also started avoiding social gatherings that require traveling or being in unfamiliar locations. Over time, this avoidance has strained his relationships with colleagues and friends who no longer understand why he is so withdrawn. Ali’s interactions with Leila have been profoundly affected as well. While he wants to support her recovery, his own anxiety often leads him to overcompensate by monitoring every aspect of her life, which can feel suffocating for her. The constant replaying of the traumatic event in his mind makes it difficult for Ali to engage fully with their daily lives or plan for the future. What finally brought Ali to seek help was a realization that these symptoms were worsening and affecting both his professional and personal relationships. He is most afraid of losing control, of being unable to protect Leila or maintain his role as a supportive husband and colleague. Yet, he also harbors hope that with the right support, he can regain some semblance of normalcy in his life. Ali’s journey towards healing is one of acknowledging the profound impact of trauma on his daily existence and recognizing the need for professional guidance to navigate these challenges.
